visuals.title: Quiz
visuals.text: Five questions. Answer along on the cards below the transcript, then hear Marco's answers.

quiz.pause_at: Pause here if you want to think it through

questions.q: In a 90-second Star story, where should most of the time go?

options.text: The situation, so they see the context
The result, so they remember it
The action, in the first person
The team, and what we achieved

questions.explain: About 50 of the 90 seconds go on what you did and why, in the first person. Sofia's first try spent almost all of it on the situation and said "we".
questions.explain_at: Fifty for the action, in the first person

questions.q: What's missing from "I love finance and I like a fast pace" as an answer to why banking?

options.text: Anything specific to you
An honest mention of the pay
A list of the bank's big deals
More enthusiasm for the pace

questions.explain: Every candidate could say it. Give a moment that drew you in and the evidence behind it, so the interviewer learns something about you.
questions.explain_at: That's true of every candidate in the building

questions.q: What makes a strong answer to "why this bank?"

options.text: Its place at the top of the league tables
The size of the deals it works on
Praise for its brand and reputation
Evidence you gathered, linked to your story

questions.explain: A person you spoke to, or a deal they advised on that you followed, tied back to what you've said about yourself. League tables are what the bank's own website says.
questions.explain_at: The strong answer has evidence only you could have

questions.q: Why did it matter whether Daimler-Benz and Chrysler was called a merger or a takeover?

options.text: A merger needed no shareholder vote
Takeover targets expect a control premium
A takeover would have been blocked
Mergers pay the target in cash

questions.explain: In a takeover the buyer pays extra to take charge; in a merger of equals nobody does. Kerkorian argued a takeover had been sold as a merger.
questions.explain_at: in a takeover the target's shareholders expect a control premium

questions.q: Tesco's Czech and Slovak businesses have an enterprise value of €1.7bn, but Tesco expects about €1.2bn of net cash. What explains most of the gap?

options.text: Tax on the gain from the sale
The Hungarian business it keeps
Lease liabilities counted as debt
Synergies Ahold expects to earn

questions.explain: The €1.7bn counts the stores' leases as debt, under IFRS 16; leave them out and it's €1.2bn. The cash figure is before tax.
questions.explain_at: The one point seven counts the stores' leases as debt
